paragraphs.source_en: The location of painted shelters within stone cities varies. For example at Aouarnhat painted shelters occur in the whole stone city but the largest compositions are located on walls facing the outside of the site. They are thus–intentionally–exposed towards the outside and they are visible from faraway. On the other hand, paintings at In Itinen en bas are concentrated in the inside of the stone city and they are not visible from outside the site. A common fact in the case of paintings inside a stone city is that whereas there are suitable shelters in the external part of the city, they are empty. Assuming that the erosion of (possible) images can be excluded, this may indicate the intention to locate the paintings in a hidden position. In some sites the paintings are present both on the external part as well as hidden in the interior of the stone city.

paragraphs.source_en: In wadies, all the shelters face the ancient river course and they can be situated either in the lower part on the bottom of the wadi, or in a higher position above the wadi. Their visibility depends on how narrow the wadi is and how high its banks are, but they are usually visible at a distance. The wadies are generally easily accessible; large enough to walk inside and they are only slightly curved which makes navigation very easy.

paragraphs.source_en: Navigation inside the stone cities depends on their morphology. Some of them have large corridors where finding painted shelters is rather easy since they are visible from different points. Other stone cities consist of very narrow and curved corridors forming true labyrinths. In such sites paintings are often placed in the very internal part, so that one cannot find them unless one knows the exact way leading to them. It is easy to get lost before reaching the painted walls which suggests that the intention was to place the paintings in a safe, hidden place.
